description:
Concurrency has no acceptance or CI coverage at all.

- UAT: no config under tests/uat/configs/*.yaml runs a `throughput` or
  concurrent phase. Every config's phases are preflight -> execute -> validate
  -> package -> report, and `execute` runs single-stream power-style
  workloads. `make uat-stress` sweeps the PLATFORM MATRIX, not concurrent
  query streams. `release-gate-03-docker-oltp.yaml` sounds concurrency-related
  but runs single-stream.
- CI: no workflow runs the throughput phase or a concurrency test selection.
  The `concurrency:` keys in .github/workflows/test.yml and nightly.yml are
  GitHub Actions cancel-in-progress groups, not test concurrency. The `stress`
  pytest marker marks EXPENSIVE tests generically, not concurrency load tests,
  and default suites exclude it.

So a regression that breaks multi-stream execution (or silently drops to 2
streams, per throughput-stream-count-wiring-defect) would ship green. Add real
acceptance + CI coverage on top of the new real-DB tests.

deferrals.summary:
NEW DEFECT DISCOVERED DURING THIS TODO'S VERIFICATION (out of this
TODO's scope_limit to fix -- benchbox/core/ is not in
scope_limit.only_modify): TPC-H throughput mode fails row-count
validation for queries 11, 16, 18, and 20 on EVERY stream, at SF=1 on
DuckDB, regardless of --seed choice (reproduced with seed=42, seed=7,
and no seed at all). Confirmed independent of concurrency: the
identical 4 queries fail identically in single-stream POWER mode with
a non-reference seed; POWER mode with no seed (qgen-defaults, exact
validation against the official answer files) passes cleanly. Root
cause hypothesis: benchbox/core/tpch/throughput_test.py derives each
stream's per-query seed as `seed + stream_id * 1000 + position`, so no
throughput stream (beyond possibly the first query of stream 0) can
ever land on the reference-seed exact-match path; every throughput
query therefore falls back to LOOSE (+-50%) tolerance
(benchbox/core/expected_results/tpch_results.py), which is not wide
enough for these 4 TPC-H-spec-sanctioned non-deterministic queries.
tpch_results.py's own docstring flags RANGE mode as "reserved for
future use" and not yet wired up for TPC-H -- likely the intended fix.
Previously invisible because the throughput driver was only ever
tested against Mock connections before throughput-real-db-integration-tests,
and that TODO's new SF=0.01 tests don't hit this SF=1-scale manifestation.
Flagged as a background task (task_c4fffdd0) for a follow-up session
with full repro details and a docstring typo also noticed in passing
(tpch_results.py misstates the reference seed's decimal value).

work_units.notes:
Added tests/uat/configs/uat-throughput-duckdb-nightly.yaml: DuckDB,
TPC-H, SF=1 (the smallest TPC-compliant rung -- `run-official`, the
only CLI surface with a real --streams option, hard-rejects
non-TPC-compliant scale factors), phases_arg "load,throughput",
streams=3 (intentionally above the driver's 2-stream floor -- see w2 --
so the cell actually exercises "was my N-stream request honored?"
rather than "did the floor's default of 2 happen to match?"). Loads
cleanly via tests.uat.config.load_config (verified live).
work_units.summary: Add a UAT config that runs a real throughput phase on DuckDB (small SF, N streams)

work_units.notes:
Resumed and verified an interrupted prior attempt's changes (all kept,
none discarded -- see the completion-session's PARTIAL_WORK_DISPOSITION
for the full audit): tests/uat/config.py (execute.official/streams/seed
+ TPC-compliant-scale validation), tests/uat/matrix.py
(benchbox_run_official_argv, since `benchbox run` has no --streams
option at all -- only the deprecated `run-official --streams N`
reaches BenchmarkConfig.concurrency, via
run_official.py::_forward_requested_streams), tests/uat/runner.py
(run_cell(official=, streams=, seed=) routes through run-official and
resolves its result JSON by filename+mtime, since it has no --quiet
flag), tests/uat/phases/execute.py (threads config.execute.official/
streams/seed into the runner call), and tests/uat/throughput.py (new
module: resolve_official_result_path,
validate_stream_count/validate_throughput_metric/validate_throughput_result).

Split validate_throughput_result into two independently callable checks
(validate_stream_count, validate_throughput_metric) during this
completion pass: this TODO's own live verification surfaced a genuine,
pre-existing, orthogonal TPC-H throughput correctness defect (see
`deferred` below) that blocks a clean Throughput@Size on DuckDB at SF=1
regardless of seed. Splitting lets a caller (the nightly job, see w3)
hard-gate on the concurrency-wiring signal this TODO actually protects
(validate_stream_count) independent of that separately-tracked defect.

Added tests/uat/test_throughput.py (18 new fast unit tests: result-path
resolution incl. platform/benchmark/mtime filtering, both split
validators, the composed validator, and a drift guard against
run_official.py's TPC_ALLOWED_SCALE_FACTORS constant).
work_units.summary: Teach the UAT execute phase / matrix to run a throughput mode and validate Throughput@Size > 0 and stream count == requested

work_units.notes:
.github/workflows/nightly.yml: new `throughput-uat` job. Step 1 (hard
gate, no continue-on-error): `pytest tests/integration -k "throughput
and duckdb" -m integration` -- 5/5 pass today, exercises the real
production driver directly against a real DuckDB connection. Step 2:
`make uat-sweep CONFIG=tests/uat/configs/uat-throughput-duckdb-nightly.yaml`
(continue-on-error: true, with an inline comment explaining the tracked
defect this defers to -- see `deferred`). Step 3 (hard gate, no
continue-on-error): a short inline script calling
tests.uat.throughput.resolve_official_result_path +
validate_stream_count directly against the exported result JSON, so a
FUTURE regression that drops the requested stream count still fails
the job outright, independent of step 2's known-defect leniency.
work_units.summary: Add a nightly CI job that runs the real-DB throughput integration tests and the DuckDB throughput UAT cell
